references.text: Midian and their allies are mentioned as enemies of Israel, just as the Midianites attacked Israel in the time of the Judges.
The Midianites are described as enemies who plagued Israel, providing background for the conflict during the period of the Judges.
Abraham's descendants through Keturah, including Midian, settled in the east and became known as 'the children of the east' (בְנֵי־קֶדֶם).
The Amalekites attacked Israel, and they continued to be enemies, just as they were with the Midianites during Gideon's time.
The same coalition of Midian, Amalek, and the children of the east gathered against Israel, confirming the repeated pattern of attack.
The description of Midian, Amalek, and the children of the east lying in the valley like locusts shows the scale of the invasion.
The army of the children of the east numbered 120,000 men, showing the size of the threat Israel faced annually.
The curse that foreign peoples would harvest what Israel sown is fulfilled in the Midianites' plundering of the crops.
The curse that enemies would eat what Israel sown corresponds to what the Midianites did when Israel had sown.
